title: Late Breaking Results: A Diffusion-Based Framework for Configurable and Realistic Multi-Storage Trace Generation
problem: Existing storage trace generation methods lack the ability to produce realistic, configurable, and diverse multi-device traces that capture temporal dynamics and inter-device dependencies with high fidelity.
motivation: Accurate, controllable storage traces are essential for characterizing and evaluating storage system behavior, and current synthetic generators do not reliably produce traces matching real-world patterns.
method: DiTTO uses diffusion models to synthesize high-fidelity continuous traces that capture temporal dynamics and inter-device dependencies. The framework allows user-defined configurations while maintaining fidelity to real storage patterns, achieving trace generation with only 8% configuration errors.
key_novelty: Application of diffusion-based generative models to multi-storage trace synthesis with configurable parameters and high temporal realism.
contributions: DiTTO framework leveraging diffusion models for storage trace generation
Support for user-defined configuration guidance in trace generation
High-fidelity synthesis capturing temporal dynamics and inter-device dependencies
Generation with only 8% configuration error rates
primary_theme: Diffusion-based generative models for realistic storage workload synthesis
